newsitem.title: USA: Yankees owner considers selling stock - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yankees owner considers selling stock - paper.

text.p: The owner of the New York Yankees, who wants a new stadium for the team that won the World Series on Sunday, is considering selling $200 million of stock, the New York Post said in its Friday edition.

The paper only quoted principal owner George Steinbrenner as saying "It's an interesting idea." However, it reported that another source, identified as a Yankee insider, as saying "Going public may be the only way to go," as New York Gov. George Pataki might not be willing to commit public funds to a new stadium.
The plan likely would involve having the Yankees first organize a bond issue, secure the land for the new stadium, and then do an initial public offering, according to the New York Post's source.
The paper said the proceeds also could be used to refurbish the historic, 73-year old stadium in the Bronx, but called this a less likely alternative.

The New York Times, in its Thursday edition, said that U.S. Senator Al D'Amato, R-NY, who can play a major role in local politics, was opposed to one of the options being considered, building a new stadium on Manhattan's West Side.

The paper quoted the senator as saying "I don't think in my lifetime." D'Amato added "I'm not passing judgment as it relates to the merits. I just make the observation that I think it's very doubtful given all the hurdles that would have to be cleared, particularly the community and the environment. It would be difficult if not impossible."
